News.title: Terrifying moment huge dust storm wall sweeps across city and plunges thousands into darkness
News.content:
THIS is the moment a massive dust storm engulfed northwestern India, turning daylight into near-darkness.

Footage shows a dense yellow cloud of dust advancing towards the city of Bikaner, in Rajasthan – just like a scene from The Mummy.





Made up of fine sand and mineral particles, the dust cast an apocalyptic glow over streets and homes.

The storm’s ferocity caused widespread disruption across Bikaner since it first appeared this afternoon local time.

Visibility dropped sharply, forcing drivers to abandon their cars on the road and shopkeepers to shut their businesses as panic spread through crowded markets.

Power cuts were reported in several areas, while tree branches snapped under the force of the winds.

The Jaipur Meteorological Center has warned of more severe weather across Rajasthan.

Thunderstorms and powerful winds reaching 37–45 miles an hour are expected in Bikaner, Jaipur, Ajmer, Bharatpur, Kota, Jodhpur, and Udaipur divisions.

Two orange alerts – a severe weather warning – for hailstorms have been issued by India’s Meteorological Department, set to last until Sunday.

Forecasters also said the cycle of afternoon storms is likely to continue for four to five days.



Authorities have urged people to stay indoors during extreme conditions and avoid unnecessary travel until the weather stabilises.

Dust storms are a very common weather phenomenon in India, mostly in the arid and semi-arid regions of the north-west and the Indo-Gangetic Plains.

They occur most frequently during the pre-monsoon summer months – from March through June – before the annual monsoon rains arrive.

Earlier this month, at least 96 people were killed by dust storms, heavy rain and lightning in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.

Another 50 were injured, while a number of homes and other structures were heavily damaged.



Officials said that many deaths were caused by falling trees, collapsing structures and lightning.

In Prayagraj district, residents were in panic as strong winds tore through neighbourhoods.

Local resident Ram Kishore said: “The storm came suddenly, and the sky turned completely dark within minutes.

“Tin roofs were flying, and people ran indoors. We could hear trees falling throughout the evening.”

In the neighbouring Bhadohi district, Savitri Devi said her family narrowly escaped after strong winds damaged their mud house.

“We rushed outside when the walls started shaking because of the wind,” she said.

“Our roof collapsed moments later. We spent the night at a relative’s house.”

News.title: Andy Burnham is “wargaming” holding a snap general election if he becomes PM
News.content:
ANDY Burnham is considering holding a snap general election if he becomes PM, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

He is also lining up Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood to be his Chancellor, Labour insiders believe.



Mr Burnham is the narrow favourite to win the Makerfield by-election next month and make a bombshell return to Westminster.



He will then challenge Sir Keir Starmer for the leadership and keys to No10 – declaring only he can beat Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.

Some in Team Burnham think he should capitalise on Labour’s expected poll bounce to call an early election.

This would let him get his own mandate from voters to enact radical policies in No10, they believe.

But others in his camp have warned him that Labour MPs will not tolerate an early election as many would expect to lose their seats – even if the party gets a majority.

A senior Labour source said: “Andy considering an early general election. They are wargaming it.

“But Labour MPs would absolutely hate it. They are worried about losing their seats.

“If Andy becomes PM I expect he will have to promise the PLP (Parliamentary Labour Party) that he will not call a snap election.



“They will want him to sign the pledge in blood.”

The Greater Manchester Mayor is the narrow favourite to win the Makerfield by-election next month and make his long-anticipated return to Westminster.

He will then challenge Sir Keir for the Labour leadership. He could be PM by summer, despite not even standing on Labour’s landslide winning 2024 manifesto.

Mr Burnham has used his appearances on the campaign trail to launch a string of fiery attacks on Sir Keir and the way Labour and the country have been run for generations.

The wannabe PM has said Britain has been on the “wrong path” of “neolibersliam” for the past 40 years and called for more state control of industries.



He has also called for Labour to get back in touch with its working class roots.

The Sun on Sunday understands that Mr Burnham and his team have started drawing up plans for his first months as PM.

Buckingham Palace has reportedly been contacted to check they would not have any objections if another King’s Speech was held this year.

A new PM would have to pen another King’s Speech if they wanted to bring in different Bills and policies.

Mr Burnham is expected to carry out a sweeping Cabinet reshuffle if he does seize Downing Street.



Ms Mahmood, the current Home Secretary, is expected to be made Chancellor.

She was one of the Cabinet ministers who went in to see Sir Keir in No10 and told him to set out a timetable to quit in showdown talks earlier this month.

The Sun on Sunday has been told that talks between Shabana’s team and Mr Burnham had been going on for a while.

Lucy Powell and Angela Rayner are both expected to be brought back into the Cabinet with big jobs.

Mr Burnham is being advised by Sue Gray – Sir Keir’s former chief of staff who was fired from the job after only a few months.



Her treatment sparked accusations that Starmer’s regime was running a “boys club”

A senior party source said: “Shabana is meant to have done a deal with Andy to be his Chancellor.

“That is why she let it be known she had told Keir to go. She was manoeuvring to get a big job.”

Josh Simons, the Labour MP who quit his Makerfield seat so Mr Burnham could have a shot at returning to Westminster, is also expected to get a job.



Insiders believe Mr Simons is expecting to get out into Downing Street in a big policy job, but is more likely to be put in the House of Lords.

Mr Burnham’s team declined to comment.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Source close to Shabana said: “Nonsense. There are no deals being made.

“Shabana is entirely focused on her job as Home Secretary.”

News.title: Hikers warned as dozens fall sick on popular trail with one airlifted to hospital from highly contagious virus
News.content:
DOZENS of hikers have fallen sick on a popular trail from a highly contagious virus.

One man was so unwell he had to be airlifted to hospital as officials scramble to find the source of the spread.





Around two dozen illnesses have been reported over the past few weeks on a section of the Pacific Crest Trail in California.

First reports were made to officials on May 8 with at least seven hikers being diagnosed with norovirus, SFGate reported.

The vomiting virus is highly contagious and spreads through contaminated food, water, or surfaces.

Retiree Ron Hals, 73, from Fort Bragg, California, became violently sick while camping on the trail on May 14.



“I’ve never been that weak,” he told the news outlet, saying he was finding it difficult to stand.

“When I finally managed to fall asleep the next morning, I didn’t even take my shoes off or cover myself with a blanket.”

Fellow hikers alerted medics who dispatched the helicopter to take him to hospital where he was diagnosed with the bug.

“The PCTA is aware of reports of gastrointestinal illness in the Wrightwood area,” the Pacific Crest Trail Association said.



“We are working with the San Bernardino County Department of Public Health as they assess the situation.

“We intend to share information publicly as soon as it is available.”

Hals believes he contracted the virus while getting supplies in Wrightwood, a key access point for the trail.

Others suggested to SFGATE that a water cache in Swarthout Valley could be the culprit.

On Wednesday, PTCA officials told PEOPLE said “at this stage, it is too early to characterize the full extent of the situation or identify a confirmed source.”



The U.S. Sun has contacted the PCTA for an update.

Norovirus can be fatal due to the dehydration that can occur with severe diarrhea and vomiting which usually show up 24 to 48 hours after contact.

Trail officials have told hikers to be extra cautious in the coming weeks with frequent hand washing, no sharing of food or utensils, treating drinking water, and leaving the trail if symptoms arise.

News.title: Tragedy as baby dies after being rushed to hospital as man & woman arrested
News.content:
DEATH PROBE Tragedy as baby dies after being rushed to hospital as man & woman arrested

A BABY has tragically died after being rushed to hospital with cops arresting a man and woman.

Cops and emergency services were called to a property in Gateshead, Tyne and Wear, over concerns for the welfare of a baby on Thursday afternoon.



The baby was taken to hospital but sadly died a short time later, Northumbria Police said.

A man was arrested on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child.



Cops confirmed that a woman has been arrested on suspicion of neglect.

The two were released on bail pending further enquiries.

The force asked people to “avoid speculation” with the investigation underway.

Officers are said to be “taking the necessary time to establish the circumstances”.

A spokesperson for Northumbria Police said: “Shortly after 1.45pm yesterday (Thursday), we received a report via the ambulance service of concern for the welfare of a baby in the Gateshead area.

“The baby was taken to hospital but tragically died a short time later.

“Our thoughts are with their loved ones at this time.

“We immediately launched an investigation, and two people have been arrested in connection with the report.



“A man has been arrested on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child, and a woman has been arrested on suspicion of neglect.

“Both have been released on police bail pending further enquiries.

“The investigation is very much at an early stage, and we would ask people to avoid speculation as officers take the necessary time to establish the circumstances.”

News.title: Farmer, 65, killed by rampaging wild elephant as terrified locals plan protests after string of horror deaths
News.content:
DEADLY ATTACK Farmer, 65, killed by rampaging wild elephant as terrified locals plan protests after string of horror deaths

A FARMER has tragically died after attempting to chase a wild elephant away from his home.

Pullerkatt Mohanan, 65, lost his life when the wild beast turned on him in the early hours of Saturday morning after his neighbours raised the alarm.





Locals say the rampaging elephant had been at the property the night before, damaging the family’s crops.

After attempting to drive the animal away from his home in Vaysery, Athirappilly, Kerala, it suddenly charged towards him around 2.40am.

Mohanan was left critically injured in the clash.

In the aftermath, he was rushed to Chalakudy Taluk Hospital and then to a private facility.



But despite doctors’ best efforts, he was unable to be saved.

Forest officials confirmed that Mohanan, his brother Rathessh and another relative had tried to ward off the elephant in the moments prior to the attack.

The elephant retreated into the jungle following the horrific ordeal.

Patrol teams have since been deployed to ensure the creature does not return.



Mohanan’s death marks the sixth fatal elephant attack in the Athirappilly region this year.

Just days ago, a 62-year-old man was killed in a similar incident nearby.

Locals say they live in constant fear of elephants.

They say the beasts damage their crops and property when they enter residential areas.

Authorities have promised immediate financial assistance to Mohanan’s family.



But residents have accused the government of failing to deliver support or solutions despite repeated assurances of stronger protection measures.

Athirappilly is known for its forests and waterfalls and has long faced clashes between humans and wildlife.

Experts say shrinking forest cover and farming near reserve boundaries have a major influence on the increasing numbers of elephants straying into residential areas.

Claiming the government had been negligent, villagers organised a massive protest in Athirappilly for Saturday and announced they will block the Chalakudy-Anamalai interstate highway.

News.title: I was hung naked from the ceiling & whipped by Taliban torturers – their evil games convinced me I was living in a box
News.content:
SQUINTING ahead at his Taliban captors, aid worker Kevin Cornwell could see an AK-47, a video camera and a small yellow sticky note.

On the latter, written in misspelt English, was the false claim that he was a British spy. Over a horrifying 272-day ordeal, he would come to learn the depths of their torturous games, as he was locked in with rapists and “organ snatchers” and left convinced he was only leaving “in a box”.



Accused of plotting an act of terrorism and instructed to read the note aloud, Kevin, from Middlesborough, knew refusing would lead to another round of vicious abuse, which saw him hung naked from a ceiling, pummelled with pipes and whipped with cables.



For nearly a year, he was imprisoned on false charges by the Taliban in their bid for money, prisoner swaps and to get the Government around the negotiating table.

He suffered beatings from guards, physical clashes with Islamist extremists desperate to convert and radicalise him and the threat of public execution, fatal stabbing and shooting.

Eventually, Kevin was released, alongside other three Brits, in October 2023 after an alleged £120million payment from the Government. He still vividly recalls his traumatic experiences.

Kevin tells us: “There were times where I thought, there’s no way I’m ever getting out of here.

“The interrogation, the indoctrination, the interviews, the traumatic, brutal ways they were terrorising and torturing me, I thought the only way I’m leaving is in a box.



“My main hope was my wife Kelly, who told me, ‘One way or another, I’m getting you home’. I knew she would do whatever she could.”

Kevin was working for the UN Refugee agency, as a project manager and medic, when he was interrogated by and arrested by secret police in Kabul, Afghanistan, back in January 2023.

After being summoned to his hotel, he was “frogmarched to his room”, which had been “ransacked and turned upside down”, and quizzed over a pistol in the safe.

He had a licence, it was to be used in the event of a terror attack, but officers denied it existed. They also stole $12,000 from his safe and confiscated all IT equipment.

A bag was placed over Kevin’s head and he was driven to a compound where he would be held for the next nine months “under stress and duress as they tried to break me”.



In his first interrogation, he was on his knees with his hands cuffed behind his back. Any answers they didn’t like were met with a rifle butt hit to the back of the head.

They showed him AK-47s, magazines with “lots of ammo”, wires, radios and other devices he didn’t recognise. They claimed he planned to use it for a terror attack.

“You are a terrorist, you’ve come here to hurt the Taliban for the British Government,” they told him.

After refuting the claims, he was beaten again, hooded and taken to an underground cage in solitary confinement where he was held for 11 days.

Apart from a daily toilet break, his only contact was when guards would enter to whip him with plastic tubing, fight him or threaten to stab him “for their own amusement”.



Radicalisation plot

It was all part of a plan to wear Kevin down to comply with their demands, as her discovered in the “next stage of captivity” inside a cell with five jihadists.

“These were extremely violent people, who spent three months solidly trying to break me physically and mentally and radicalise me,” he says.

“At times they would randomly jump on me and attack me, it was hard fighting off five of them but I can handle myself, and when I did win guards would beat me with sticks

“They would say things like ‘The Christian world is no more,’ and ‘There are too many Muslims around the world, all Christians will die’ – always in broken English.

“When they weren’t praying, which was five times a day, they would take it in turns to continuously preach the Quran in front of me and try to convert me to Islam.



I decided if I was going to die I’d rather be awake for my final moments Kevin Cornwell

“These were people who had murdered people and whole families, rapists and those who had taken children to sell them for their organs.

“They wanted to convert me because it would get them a free pass into heaven, they would say, ‘Allah will let me go there, I will have virgins and be accepted.’”

During that time, he was taken for more interrogations where he was grilled about his former career – nearly 25 years in the military including 12 years in the Royal Army Medical Corp – for “anything to use against me as leverage”.

They held him at gunpoint and instructed him to read notes claiming he was a terrorist, a British spy, and how bad the British and American Governments were.

The only time he would comply was when it was written in poor English and he would mispronounce words to indicate something was wrong.



“I would state it exactly as it was on the sticky notes, one was ‘I ham Kefin off br-tish intel agent’. Another was, ‘I had work in Afghanistan for the br-tish gov-ment.’

“Instead I would keep saying that I worked in Kabul for the UN as a project manager and medic, needless to say I took a beating again for that.”

‘They broke me physically’

When sending the videos to their commanders, the guards would realise the mistakes and fume “Why you not speak like English?” and “This is not like TV”.

“The Taliban commander told me, ‘You’re not making it easy’. I said, ‘I’m not here to make it easy’,” he recalls. “I tried to make it very difficult for them.

“While they broke me many times physically, mentally I was unbreakable. That annoyed them and that’s why they tortured me in the way they did.



“In a final interview, they threatened to charge me with espionage, which under the Taliban was punishable by public execution.”

Kevin was moved between multiple cells after but his health was declining, he was hospitalised with sepsis twice during his incarceration.



He had previously suffered with kidney stones and due to not having medication it was worsening. The beatings only exacerbated the damage to his organs.

The first time he was taken to a hospital, which was run by the Taliban, it was “the most disgusting environment” Kevin had ever seen.

His one kidney was blocked because of the amount of stones in it and required an operation, but he refused the offer of anaesthetic and demanded an epidural.

“I decided if I was going to die I’d rather be awake for my final moments,” he says.

The Taliban captors were brutal and Kevin recalls them becoming even more violent when it came to torturing local prisoners.



He recalls: “One local had clips put on his genitalia and different parts of his body and was electrocuted. We heard his loud screams.

“When he was thrown back into the cell, the guards said he had gone mad but they had broken him. He had burnt tissue all over his body.

These were people who had murdered people and whole families, rapists and those who had taken children to sell them for their organs Kevin Cornwell

“Others were tortured to the point where they nearly died.

“They would suffocate them by hanging until their last moments, then release them and would start it again. That’s how violent it was.”

Coded messages

At times, Kevin felt hopeless and feared the only way he would leave the prison was inside a wooden box.



But 5,000 miles away, his wife Kelly was fiercely fighting to get him home by any means necessary.

Despite being told not to speak to the media, she appeared on TV in a bid to “humanise Kevin”, get the public behind her battle and put pressure on the Government to act.

She was only able to speak to her husband six times during his incarceration, which Kevin used to relay coded messages – which they agreed during his military career – that could be fed back to authorities.

He says: “If I spoke about Benidorm, which I disliked with a passion, she knew I meant the opposite in anything I said after, so ‘People are being really nice today’ would be reversed.”

Kevin found solace through meditation – eventually able to spend up to 10 hours at a time doing it – and “thinking about home” to distract himself from mental anguish and physical pain.



In September, Taliban officials began to give hope to Kevin by telling him American prisoners would be released first, followed by Brits, after their governments paid up.

In the early hours of October 9, he was handcuffed and a bag was placed on his head. Kevin and other Brits were escorted to a military vehicle to the airport.

Kevin says £120million was paid for the release of multiple prisoners.

Before leaving, he was warned: “Don’t come back to this country, you’re blacklisted. If you come back, we can’t assure your safety.”



Twisted tyrants

Reuniting with Kelly at Heathrow Airport, he broke down in tears. The ordeal was finally over but he sustained mental and physical scars which he has battled through.

He needed two operations on his kidneys, which were only functioning 25 and 75 per cent, due to the damage caused by the Taliban and his medication being withheld.

At first he was sensitive to noisy environments and light. Kevin adds: “Even now I prefer to sit in the dark now, it’s more calming for me.”

Now Kevin and Kelly mentor and coach others suffering from domestic abuse, stress and mental health related conditions – they’ve also counselled other wrongly imprisoned people and their families.



“We try to give back in any way we can by helping people who need our support, it all stems from what we went through,” he adds.

They say they have undergone “post-traumatic growth” – experiencing a positive psychological change in response to traumatic experiences.

“I think everything I’ve been through it’s made me a stronger, more adaptable person,” Kevin says.

The one keepsake from his time incarcerated is a makeshift toothbrush, which was gifted to him by a kind 18-year-old guard.

He stores it in a cupboard drawer and regularly looks as a reminder of the goodness in the world, even amid the “brutality and trauma” he suffered at the hands of his Taliban captors.



Remarkably, Kevin, who’s a father of seven and grandfather of 18, says he would return to Afghanistan tomorrow to continue his humanitarian work, if the Taliban weren’t in control.

“I love the country and the people are phenomenal, loving and caring. The tyrants out there are causing significant difficulties to their own people, which is terrible and really disheartening.”

News.title: We were raped in a drug-induced sleep like Gisele Pelicot… sick ‘academies’ are teaching Brits how to commit vile abuse
News.content:
MUM-OF-FOUR Zoe Watts and her husband had just returned from church when he tentatively put his hand on her knee and told her he had a confession to make.

“I’ve been putting sleeping tablets in your tea, then having sex with you while you were unconscious,” he told her.





As devastated Zoe tried to come to terms with his admission, her now ex-husband begged for help for what he labelled a mental health issue. It would be months before Zoe realised what he was actually talking about was rape.

Zoe and a second victim Amanda Stanhope have now launched a campaign to raise awareness of the terrifying phenomenon which charity workers have told The Sun is becoming “widespread”.

And statistics show five per cent of Britain’s 2.2million adult rape victims – around 110,000 – believe they were sedated in some way before being attacked.

It follows the emergence of sick online sites where twisted men share tips on how to sedate partners, boasting of filming their sleeping loved ones and swapping details of effective drugs and doses.

The unspeakable nature of the crime was highlighted by the case of French woman Gisèle Pelicot who was systematically drugged and raped by her husband and dozens of strangers he recruited online.

Zoe and Amanda are among “hundreds of women” who have faced the same ordeal and many claim they were badly let down by authorities who KNEW they were being abused – but didn’t act quickly enough.

Zoe, 43, claims her husband, who is serving 11 years for rape, sexual assault by penetration and drugging, told at least three health professionals what he was doing – but it was only reported to police when her mum stepped in.

While doctors and mental health workers have a professional duty to report safeguarding concerns in the UK there is no law which dictates they must.





Fellow campaigner Amanda was fobbed off by police after reporting her partner. She spent more than two years waiting for him to be charged – only to discover cops hadn’t submitted vital files to CPS.

Zoe, of Devon, said: “It’s a crime that nobody wants to believe goes on.

“I felt like there was a sort of societal cover up, that I wasn’t a victim, that this was his illness and I had to support this poor man. I wouldn’t leave him if he had diabetes or cancer, so why would I leave him for this?

“We even went to marriage counselling and I remember him sitting with his head in his hands distressed. I was trying to make sense of it all but was told to give him time and space.

“He was involved with at least three health professionals and none of them reported it as a safeguarding issue – they were only interested in what he presented as his problem.”

Zoe, who was sedated with her son’s sleeping medication over a five-year period until her husband’s arrest in 2018, said: “The day he told me we’d been to church.

“It was a service about the different ways God can love you. He put his hand on my knee and said, ‘I need to talk to you later’.

“We went on to have a normal Sunday afternoon and I didn’t think anything of it. When the kids went to bed we sat down in the lounge and explained he’d been putting our son’s sleeping medication in my tea at night.

“He said he was doing it to tie me up and restrain me, to take video footage and photograph himself having sex with me.”



It was months before Zoe realised she was the victim of a real crime.

She said: “He was this church-going man, known to his community as Mr Wonderful with his great wife and kids. For a while I didn’t want to think it was possible that my husband could do such heinous things.”

It was only when Zoe told her family what was going on that her mum made a complaint to police and her husband was jailed in 2022.

Amanda, who was on prescription drugs which knocked her out at night, claims she could have been raped 1,000 times by ex-partner David Rogerson while she slept.

Sickeningly, one attack followed Rogerson discovering her unconscious in a hotel room following a sleeping pill overdose.

He put her in bed, called 999 and then raped her while waiting for the ambulance to arrive. It was the first time she awoke during one of his depraved attacks.

“I remember being slapped so hard that I came around,” Amanda says. “I was face down on the bed. I couldn’t actually move, I couldn’t speak because of the medication I’d taken.

“He was on top of me, slapping me, raping me. I felt my whole self shatter and fragment into a million pieces. I didn’t know if I was alive, dead or dying.”



It took officers at Greater Manchester Police two years and three months to charge him due to “negligence and mishandling paperwork”.

Amanda told us: “What the police put me through was as bad as the abuse. I thought he would be charged within six months.

“They had my medical records, all this information and even a confession from him saying, ‘I’m really sorry I won’t do it again.’

“I felt like an inconvenience. I was constantly asking for an update but was fobbed off.”

Rogerson hanged himself in May last year and an inquest ruled death by misadventure. His death came six weeks after he was bailed ahead of making a plea in court but he had always denied abusing her.

Amanda, 52, of Wigan, received an apology from Greater Manchester Police, who she says “caused psychological harm” due to their handling of the case.

The force acknowledged their actions led to a “severe relapse in PTSD, suicidal thoughts and emotional deterioration”.

They wrote: “It is deeply concerning that the trauma you are now facing is not solely from the crime itself, but from the way your case has been handled.”



Amanda also claims health workers expressed concern she “might be being abused” and gave her a leaflet about narcissistic personality disorder but feels not enough action was taken.

Amanda alleges at least one assault video of her, taken while she was sedated, and multiple images have been shared online but fears there could be more. Zoe does not know.

The pair have now launched a survivor-led campaign called #EndEyeCheck.

Its name refers to an act in which men drug and abuse unconscious women and pull back the eyelid of their victim to prove they are incapacitated before sharing images or filming as online footage.

One website, where the sickening clips were shared, boasted 62 million views in February alone and other of the so-called ‘Rape Academies’ shared methods for sedating women, along “sleeping liquids” shipped anywhere in the world for £130.

Zoe also warns ‘eyelid checks’ are mimicked on pornographic sites which promote the act.

The pair now want specific legislation to make the creation, possession and distribution of such material an offence. They also want online platforms to be punished for hosting it.

They say they have heard from hundreds of UK women who have been through the same chilling ordeal – and many say they have been let down by the justice system and professionals meant to help them.

Amanda said: “Both Zoe and I have received hundreds of messages from women all over the world. Many have asked for the signs and symptoms.

“These crimes have been reported to the police but why did nobody know about these types of crimes until Gisele Pelicot? There are a hell of a lot more cases coming up too.”



The courage of Gisele, 73, of Avignon, France, has been applauded worldwide after she waived her anonymity in a stand against her ex-husband Dominique’s depraved acts.

He was jailed for 20 years for drugging and raping her as well as inviting dozens of men to abuse her over nearly a decade. All but three of 50 other men were also found guilty of varying charges related to the attacks.

Figures from the Official of National Statistics reveal that an estimated 110,000 adults over the age of 16 believe they were drugged before being raped in the year ending March 2025.

Of that number, 1.6 per cent said it was at the hands of an ex or current partner and 5.4 per cent knew their attacker.

Ciara Bergman, CEO of Rape Crisis England & Wales, said: “We don’t know how many cases of drug-assisted rape there have been – even one is too many, but we are seeing emerge a troubling picture of widespread and largely hidden abuse, which needs urgent attention from all responsible agencies.

“Violence against women and girls has already been declared a national emergency, and cannot be addressed unless we also come to terms with rape culture, in which sexual violnece and abuse are normalised, victims are shamed and blamed, perpetrators act with almost complete impunity and the systems that are supposed to safeguard and support women too often fail and retraumatise them.”

The General Medical Council, which regulates all doctors working in the UK, said its members were expected to “act promptly” if a patient, or someone close to their patient, is “at risk of abuse or serious harm”.

A spokesperson said: “Confidential information can be disclosed without consent where failure to do so could expose others to a risk of death or serious harm, including in relation to serious crime.”



Greater Manchester Police said it regretted Amanda’s ordeal.

A spokesperson said: “It is to our regret that Ms Stanhope did not get to see justice fully served at the end of this awful ordeal. We have written to her to apologise for areas where our service fell below that she had every right to expect.”

They said changes had been made to speed up investigation timelines.

Shadow national security and safeguarding minister Alicia Kearns said: “A society that lets predators teach each other how to rape unconscious women is one where inaction has become the state’s deadliest weapon.

“These vile online rape academies cannot be allowed to operate and encourage the mass rape of women across the world.

“The Government must urgently take action to ban rape academies.”

News.title: Moment Ukrainian drones destroy Putin’s spy planes, shadow fleet tanker & nuclear-capable missile complex in £250m blow
News.content:
UKRAINIAN drones have destroyed two Russian spy planes, an oil tanker and a missile complex in a costly overnight blitz for Vladimir Putin.

The massive coordinated assault hit key targets in the port cities of Taganrog and Feodosia and is expected to have caused up to £250million in damages.





Footage showed an attack on two Tu-142 long-range anti-submarine aircraft at an airbase in the port city of Taganrog.

The Soviet-era Tu-142 is no longer in production, with the blitz of two planes estimated at an eye- watering £200million.



Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces, commanded by Robert Brovdi, coordinated the mission.

Brovdi said 23 military targets were at the centre of the operation which he described as a “fiery night”.

A state-of-the-art Iskander system – worth around £20 million – and a £30million “shadow tanker” were also taken out in the mission.

Russian authorities confirmed a drone attack damaged a facility belonging to Southern Oil Company in Armavir’s industrial zone.



Officials said emergency services were working to contain the blaze and assess the extent of the damage.

Taganrog has been targeted multiple times in recent months.

In late March 2026, a drone attack on the city killed one person and wounded eight others, authorities said.



Russia launched its own salvo of drones and ballistic missiles at Ukraine on Friday night.

Around 13,000 residents were left without electricity in Zaporizhzhia, after strikes hit energy infrastructure.

It comes after Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on Friday that Russia was preparing for a major attack.

In a post on Telegram he said: “We possess intelligence indicating that Russia is organising a new large-scale assault.

“Our services are reacting swiftly and are ready.”



Putin has maintained his claims of victory on the front line.

Earlier this week he told journalists in Kazakhstan: “Our forces are advancing on all fronts – you see it every day.”

Russia warned foreigners to leave Kyiv saying it planned a “series of systematic strikes” on its defence infrastructure.

Tensions between Moscow and Nato have also spiked after a Russian drone crashed into an apartment building in Romania on Friday.

Multiple people were left injured in the unprecedented strike as the alliance scrambled fighter jets to respond to the “serious violation”.



Putin has since issued a chilling warning to Europe that nobody “will sleep peacefully”.

News.title: Teenager dies after entering lake in Nottinghamshire in 15th heatwave water death
News.content:
Teenager dies after entering lake in Nottinghamshire in 15th heatwave water death

A 19-year-old man has tragically died after entering Balderton Lake in New Balderton, Nottinghamshire, on Thursday afternoon

View 2 Images Emergency services were called to Balderton Lake on Thursday (Image: Joseph Raynor/ Reach PLC)

A 19-year-old man has tragically died after entering a lake in Nottinghamshire, becoming the 15th person to die in water-related incidents during the recent heatwave.

‌



Police were alerted at around 2.30pm on Thursday to reports that a man had entered the water at Balderton Lake in New Balderton, near Newark.

‌



Emergency services attended the scene and pulled the 19-year-old from the water. The teenager, who had been at the lake with friends, was treated at the scene by paramedics before being taken to hospital, Nottinghamshire Live reports.

‌



In an update on Saturday, Nottinghamshire Police confirmed that the young man had sadly died. Police said his family have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers. The death is not being treated as suspicious and a file will be prepared for the coroner.

Chief Inspector Clive Collings said: "This is a tragic incident and our thoughts are solely with this young man's family. We recognise this will be very upsetting for the local community and we encourage people to access support if they need it.

"During hot weather we know people want to keep cool but open waters are exceptionally dangerous as there is no way of telling what's beneath the surface."

‌



View 2 Images Chiedza Nyanjowa, 15, tragically died after getting into difficulty in water at Formby beach on Monday (Image: Merseyside Police)

Group manager Charlotte Weatherall-Smith, from Nottinghamshire Fire and Rescue Service, said: "I would like to extend our deepest sympathies and heartfelt condolences to the family, friends and loved ones of this young man at this incredibly difficult time.

"This is a tragic incident, and our thoughts remain with everyone affected. Incidents like this are a stark reminder of the dangers that open water can present.

‌



"Even on warm and sunny days, water temperatures can be much colder than they appear, and entering the water can lead to cold water shock, which can be sudden, severe and potentially fatal.

"If you see someone in difficulty in the water, call 999 immediately and ask for the fire service. Encourage the person to float on their back to help them stay calm and conserve energy. For your own safety, please do not enter the water or attempt a rescue yourself, as this can put additional lives at risk."

News.title: Woman who put cat into wheelie bin still 'doesn't feel forgiven' 16 years later
News.content:
Woman who put cat into wheelie bin still 'doesn't feel forgiven' 16 years later

Mary Bale was a 45-year-old single bank worker who suddenly became known around the world when she was spotted on CCTV putting a cat into a wheelie bin

View 6 Images The infamous moment Mary Bale dumped a cat into a wheelie bin and became known across the world (Image: SWNS)

A woman who was hounded online after she was seen in an infamous viral video putting a cat into a bin has never “never got over her notoriety” after the incident.

‌



Mary Bale was a 45-year-old single bank worker when she was spotted in CCTV walking down a street and suddenly stopping to stroke a nearby cat. She then looked around, before suddenly grabbing the innocent cat by the neck and firmly putting the poor creature inside a wheelie bin.

‌



The incident in 2010 caused uproar online and changed Ms Bale’s life forever. The cat, Lola, was seemingly unaffected by the incident and lived a happy life until the age of 16, dying around five years ago.

‌



Still known around the world as the ‘Cat Bin Lady’, Ms Bale is reportedly now a recluse in the suburban area of Coventry, where she still lives to this day. Some of her neighbours are apparently unaware they live near a woman who was once the focus of the ire of internet users.

View 6 Images Lola the cat (Image: PA)

World Cup horror as monkeys in England shirts forced to entertain tourists READ MORE :

Her neighbour, speaking anonymously to the Daily Mail, said she has known Ms Bale through the years after the incident.

‌



“She was vilified by people across the world,” they said. “Most people have long forgotten it but not everyone and she doesn't feel forgiven.”

The source said Ms Bale resigned from her job and “never reestablished a proper career”.

They added: “She leads a very, very quiet life now and rarely speaks to anyone. I think she remains deeply embarrassed and thinks that's all she will ever be known for.”

‌



Another neighbour, Diana, said the incident had “plagued” Ms Bale and she had “never been able to live down the shame”.

View 6 Images Ms Bale was banned from owning a pet for five years (Image: PA)

Diana, who is a pet owner, said she felt sorry for Ms Bale and said that “at times she struggles”.

‌



Another neighbour also referred to Ms Bale’s father dying around the time of the furore.

They said: “Obviously it was a weird thing for her to do but when learned that her father was dying at the time - he passed just a few months later - it was clear she was not in a good place at the time she did it. Those of us who know about her are broadly sympathetic.”

At the time, Ms Bale was fined £250 at Coventry Magistrates' Court in 2021. She was ordered to pay the RSPCA's costs of £1,171 after pleading guilty to causing unnecessary suffering.

‌



Ms Bale said she did “not deserve to be hated” for what she did.

View 6 Images Lola lived happily until she was 16 (Image: Marc Daniels / newsteam.co.uk)

She said: “I really don't see what everyone is getting so excited about. It's just a cat.”

‌



She added: “I was walking home from work and saw this cat wander out in front of me. I was playing with it, stroking it and listening to it purr as it stood on a garden wall. It was very friendly.

“I don't know what came over me, but I suddenly thought it would be funny to put it in the wheelie bin, which was right beside me. I did it as a joke because I thought it would be funny. I never thought it would be trapped. I expected it to wriggle out of the bin.”

She admitted she “shouldn’t have done it” but that it was “just a cat at the end of the day” and she didn't deserve hatred from people from all around the world. She suggested her actions were “a split second of madness”.

‌



View 6 Images Ms Bale resigned from her job after 27 years (Image: Sam Furlong / SWNS.COM)

The fury grew, and a Facebook group was even set up that called for her death. Some said she was “worse than Hitler”.

Ms Bale later said she was “profoundly sorry” for what she had done.

‌



“I want to take this opportunity to apologise profusely for the upset and distress that my actions have caused,” she said. “I cannot explain why I did this, it is completely out of character and I certainly did not intend to cause any distress to Lola or her owners.

“It was a split second of misjudgement that has got completely out of control.

“I wish to reiterate that I am profoundly sorry for my actions and wish to resolve this matter to everyone's satisfaction as soon as possible.”

‌



And during the court case, defence solicitor David Murray told District Judge Caroline Goulborn said then that Ms Bale committed the "impulsive and irrational" while her father, who died between the incident and the court case, was gravely ill.

After the abuse and threats she received, Ms Bale eventually retreated into a quieter existence.

View 6 Images Ms Bale's father was gravely ill at the time (Image: CT)

Article continues below

Lola’s owners, Darryl and Stephanie, both live nearby still. They are understood to have forgiven Ms Bale, who lived a few streets away.

Ms Bale is believed to have not tried to acquire any pet since the incident. She had been banned from keeping or owning animals for five years, along with the fine she received.

News.title: Ebola outbreak Congo: WHO chief visits epicentre as virus spreads faster than response
News.content:
Ebola outbreak Congo: WHO chief visits epicentre as virus spreads faster than response

The Bundibugyo virus, the strain of Ebola currently circulating, has no approved treatment or vaccine

View 3 Images Health workers take meals to Ebola patients at the treatment centre in Rwampara (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

The head of the World Health Organisation arrived in Bunia, eastern Congo, on Saturday — a city at the centre of a rare Ebola outbreak where the virus continues to spread faster than efforts to contain it, despite improved health facilities and fresh aid deliveries.

‌



WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus is due to visit a treatment centre and hold meetings with local authorities, healthcare workers and affected families in Bunia.

‌



"The best way to address this is to provide all the necessary support to fight the disease at its epicenter and to continue offering every assistance needed," Tedros told reporters on Friday evening.

‌



The WHO confirmed on Friday that authorities have recorded 906 suspected cases and 223 suspected deaths. Neighbouring Uganda has confirmed nine cases and one death, according to the Ugandan ministry of health on Friday.

View 3 Images Director-General of the World Health Organisation (WHO), Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, speaks to the media upon his arrival at N'djili International Airport in Kinshasa, Congo (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

The Bundibugyo virus, the strain of Ebola currently circulating, has no approved treatment or vaccine.

‌



"This is a difficult situation, and we recognise that. But the Democratic Republic of Congo has faced the Ebola virus many times before. We are confident that it can once again bring this outbreak under control," Tedros told reporters on Friday, following talks with Congo's Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka. Medical aid donated by the European Union touched down in Ituri, the epicentre of Congo's Ebola outbreak, on Thursday, with further shipments anticipated over the following eight days. The US announced $80 million in additional aid on the same day, bringing its total commitment to more than $112 million.

Response efforts at Bunia's Rwampara and General hospitals appear better coordinated, with extra staff, protective equipment and medical supplies now in place, though patients continue to arrive around the clock, according to an AP reporter on Friday.

However, Doctors Without Borders, known as MSF, warned on Saturday that the response has failed to keep pace with one of the fastest-spreading outbreaks on record.

‌



"Never before has an Ebola outbreak recorded so many cases so soon after its declaration," said Dr Alan Gonzalez, MSF's deputy director of operations, in an official statement.

"Nobody knows the true scale and severity of this outbreak," Gonzalez added, urging the immediate expansion of testing, swifter deployment of aid workers and uninterrupted access for medical supplies.

View 3 Images Manza Pantience, left, a midwife at Karibuni wa Mama, supervises health workers who collect patients' samples for Ebola testing at Sofepadi Hospital in Bunia, Congo (Image: Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved)

‌



The dangers facing health workers have been further compounded by local residents' frustration over the strict medical protocols governing the handling of victims' bodies, which conflict with traditional burial customs. Residents have launched at least three attacks on health centres as a result.

Raids in Ituri by the Allied Democratic Force, a rebel group aligned with the Islamic State, along with a coalition of ethnic militias, have also hampered relief efforts. The illness has also been recorded in the Congolese provinces of North Kivu and South Kivu, south of Ituri, where the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group holds control over numerous key cities, including Goma and Bukavu. The rebels have confirmed two cases.

Uganda and Rwanda have shut their borders, while the Trump administration last week prohibited entry to non-US passport holders who had recently travelled to Congo, Uganda or South Sudan.

Article continues below

On Friday, Tedros declared border closures and travel bans "not effective at all" in halting the spread of the outbreak.

"Closing borders, as some countries have done, only discourages transparency. The Democratic Republic of Congo is reporting the situation openly and transparently," he said, urging nations to reconsider these restrictions.

News.title: Glasgow University student dies falling from bridge 'while trying to retrieve phone'
News.content:
Glasgow University student dies falling from bridge 'while trying to retrieve phone'

Thomas Reynolds, 21, is believed to have dropped his phone and lost his footing while trying to retrieve it – leading to his tragic death, as tributes pour in from family, friends and football clubs

View 2 Images Thomas Reynolds is believed to have fallen from a bridge. (Image: Instagram)

Tributes have been paid to a Glasgow University student who died after falling from a bridge. Thomas Reynolds is believed to have dropped his phone and lost his footing while attempting to retrieve it.

‌



The 21-year-old's family said he had been missing on Tuesday, 26 May, before police discovered his body the following morning. His sister Ellen paid tribute to the popular business student on Facebook.

‌



She wrote: "I'm devastated to share that my brother Thomas Reynolds was found dead in Glasgow early this morning.

‌



"He was missing all day yesterday and the police believe that he dropped his phone and tried to retrieve it but fell from the bridge and it was instant."

"Obviously my family and I are heartbroken but I know he was always very popular and many people will share our sadness and deserve to know."

Thomas played for Hutchison Vale Community Football Club as a boy and the club paid tribute to the 'caring lad' following the news of his death, reports the Daily Record.

‌



View 2 Images Thomas Reynolds has been remembered as 'a lovely, caring, popular lad'

They said: "A lovely, caring, popular lad, Tommy is a prime example to any youngster looking to work hard to develop their game. His journey is all the more incredible given he was a December birthday.

"All at Hutchison Vale FC send heartfelt condolences to his Mum Sandra, Dad Tony, sister Ellen and all of his family and friends.

‌



"Rest easy Tommy, you you were an absolute star and will be sorely missed by all the Hutchie family."

Glasgow University's football club, where Tommy played as a right back, paid tribute to a "kind soul and true friend".

A spokesperson said: "We are devastated to share the news that our right back Tommy Reynolds has passed away. Aged only 21, Tommy was studying Business at the Uni, and was a valued member of the First Team squad.

Article continues below

"Everyone that knew him realised he was a kind soul, a true friend and great teammate."

Police Scotland has been contacted for a response.

News.title: Trump labels himself the 'GOAT' in rant over cancelling USA 250th birthday celebrations
News.content:
Trump labels himself the 'GOAT' in rant over cancelling USA 250th birthday celebrations

Donald Trump thinks he should headline an upcoming festival celebrating America's 250th birthday as he claims he 'gets much larger audiences than Elvis' Presley did in his prime

View Image (Image: Getty Images)

Donald Trump is considering having a performer he claims "gets much larger audiences than Elvis in his prime" headline a festival celebrating America's 250th birthday - himself, or, as he calls himself, the "GOAT".

‌



The US president, 79, said in a Truth Social post on Saturday that he was considering headlining the Great American State Fair on the National Mall in Washington DC after a number of high-profile performers pulled out.

‌



Trump said: "I am thinking about bringing the Number One Attraction anywhere in the World, the man who gets much larger audiences than Elvis in his prime, and he does so without a guitar, the man who loves our Country more than anyone else, and the man who some say is the Greatest President in History (THE GOAT!), DONALD J. TRUMP, to take the place of these highly paid, Third Rate 'Artists'."

‌



He said he was thinking of giving a "major speech" and holding an "AMERICA IS BACK" rally in Washington DC on Wednesday, adding: "Only Great Patriots invited."

‌



Multiple performers booked for the 16-day festival - set to run from June 25 to July 10 - dropped out, with many saying they were misled about the political affiliation of the event. The festival is being organised by Freedom 250, the nonprofit created by the Trump administration.

Artists including Young MC, Morris Day, The Commodores, Bret Michaels and Martina McBride have since said they will not be taking part.

"The Commodores will not be performing at the Great American State Fair," the R&B group announced in an Instagram post on Friday. "Our music has always been our voice and we choose not to publicly affiliate with any single political party. We support the betterment of all Americans."

Article continues below

Singer McBride said in a statement on X that she was "presented with an opportunity to perform at a nonpartisan event but that turned out to be misleading".

Freedom 250 has insisted it is a nonpartisan organisation.

News.title: No justice for student who died after taking poison bought online, father says
News.content:
No justice for student who died after taking poison bought online, father says

The National Crime Agency (NCA) and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said 79 UK victims who died as a direct result of purchasing Law's products will form part of the wider case into his offending

View 2 Images Thomas was one of 79 UK victims (Image: Copyright remains with handout provider)

The father of a student who killed himself with a poison supplied by a Canadian man has said there is no "justice" for his son after prosecutors announced the seller will not face charges in the UK.

Philosophy student Thomas Parfett, 22, died in Sunbury-on-Thames, Surrey, in 2021, after taking poison bought from Kenneth Law. The 60-year-old appeared in court in Ontario, Canada, on Friday when he pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding suicide, all relating to Canadian victims.

The National Crime Agency (NCA) and the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said 79 UK victims who died as a direct result of purchasing Law's products will form part of the wider case into his offending.

View 2 Images Thomas, 22, in 2021 (Image: Copyright remains with handout provider)

Authorities informed the victims' families that Law would not face criminal proceedings in the UK because of the potential for Law to challenge the extradition after being convicted of similar offences in Canada.

Thomas's father David said the decision not to bring charges against Law in the UK was "done to me, not with me", and "in no way" brings justice for his son.

He told the Press Association: "He's not ever been charged with a crime against Tom. Yet this is the man that made £50 from selling my son a substance to kill himself, probably having persuaded him to do so, and yet he will never face charges."

He added: "It doesn't send the right message to other people that are doing the same thing, typically using internet sites."

Mr Parfett said Law was able to advertise his products online, thanks to people running "nefarious" websites in the UK.

He added that his son, a student at the University of St Andrews, accessed an online "suicide" forum before he died, where he was encouraged by other users to kill himself.

"There's others who should be prosecuted and nobody is taking the action," Mr Parfett said.

"We actually need to look at this seriously. We need to make sure that we change our processes. For instance, when you investigate a suicide of a young man like Tom, it should be a matter of course to capture the digital footprint."

The 58-year-old called for tougher internet regulations and changes to make it harder to purchase poison online.

He has joined the families of other victims to demand a public inquiry to establish the "lessons" from deaths such as Thomas's.

Mr Parfett said: "We accept things on the internet that aren't acceptable on the high street. Where else would you be able to provide somebody with detailed instructions of how to kill themselves?

"Would you walk into a bookstore to do that? I think that bookstore would be prosecuted, and yet we allow this to happen on the internet.

"Then we get ourselves into a regulatory twist about how to deal with it, while people continue to die – it's just not good enough.

"It's a complex issue, and that's why it needs the public inquiry – because you have to bring people together."

Mr Parfett, a data architect from Twickenham, south-west London, said Law did "horrendous damage" to his family, adding his son would "very likely still be here" if Law had not been trying to make money.

Since Canadian authorities dropped more serious murder charges against Law, Mr Parfett is concerned his sentence will not be tough enough.

The maximum sentence for aiding suicide in Canada is 14 years – the same as for encouraging suicide in the UK.

‌



It is understood that the sentence is likely to be more than 14 years because of the number of victims and the nature of the offences.

"I hope that he has had the chance to understand the damage he's caused," Mr Parfett said.

"I hope he is remorseful of the fact that he has exchanged lives for money. But I've not yet seen that remorse, and to me he would still remain a danger after the sentencing."

Article continues below

He added: "I'd like to be in a position to be able to forgive him. I'm not today, but I'd like to be in a position to forgive him.

"I certainly couldn't do that today, because, again, I'm not convinced he understands. But I'd like to think that he thinks about Tom sometimes."

News.title: Ed and David Miliband's mum who survived Holocaust dies aged 91 - pair share tributes
News.content:
Ed and David Miliband's mum who survived Holocaust dies aged 91 - pair share tributes

The pair paid tribute to her as 'a force field of life and love' and a 'dearly beloved mother, grandmother and sister' whose life had taken 'a remarkable trajectory'

View 2 Images David and Ed Miliband paid tribute to their mother (Image: Getty Images)

Ed and David Miliband have paid tribute to their mother after she died aged 91.

The pair announced the death of Marion Kozak, a Holocaust survivor, and left-wing campaigner on Saturday.

They paid tribute to her as “a force field of life and love” and a “dearly beloved mother, grandmother and sister”.

The siblings said: “She lived an extraordinary life with a spirit of the utmost kindness, warmth and generosity. Her life had a remarkable trajectory, from the childhood trauma of the Holocaust in Poland to safety and joy in Britain. She became a teacher, campaigner and a passionate advocate for justice. We will deeply miss her, but will carry her spirit and values with us always.”

View 2 Images Ed Miliband hailed his mum as 'remarkable' (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Born Dobra Jenta Kozak in Poland in 1934, she escaped from the Czestochowa Ghetto in 1942 during the Nazi occupation along with her mother and sister.

Article continues below

She was sheltered by nuns and then a neighbour of her aunt in Warsaw, surviving the war thanks to what her son Ed told the 2012 Labour Party conference was “the kindness of strangers”.

On an official visit to Poland in 2009 while Foreign Secretary, David Miliband paid tribute to those who had protected his mother, saying her life was “saved by those who risked theirs sheltering her from Nazi oppression”.

Ms Kozak settled in the UK after the war, marrying left-wing academic Ralph Miliband and becoming a human rights campaigner and early activist for the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament.

In his 2012 conference speech, his third as Labour leader, Ed Miliband said his mother “probably doesn’t agree with me”, but “like most mums is too kind to say so”.

But in the same speech he drew a link from her escape from the Nazis to his own political philosophy.

He said: “I believe we cannot shrug our shoulders at injustice, and just say that’s the way the world is. And I believe that we can overcome any odds if we come together as people.

Article continues below

“That’s how my mum survived the war. The kindness of strangers. Nuns in a convent who took her in and sheltered her from the Nazis, took in a Jewish girl at risk to themselves.”

News.title: Arne Slot's Liverpool sacking completes a remarkable fall from grace
News.content:
There are many questions around Slot's transfer dealings, although owners Fenway Sports Group's CEO of football Michael Edwards and sporting director Richard Hughes must also take responsibility.

Liverpool's key pair of power brokers were showered with bouquets in the summer. Now they must take the brickbats.

How did such a splurge leave an unbalanced team?

Why did Liverpool not sign competition for Mohamed Salah and Cody Gakpo on the flanks?

Was enough thought given to how Wirtz would be utilised as Liverpool revelled in beating Manchester City to his signature?

Did they really need to spend Â£125m on Isak having spent Â£70m on Ekitike?

Were they too complacent in assuming Crystal Palace would just give up on Marc Guehi?

Liverpool appeared so committed to the Isak deal, the player so exiled at Newcastle after his one-man strike to get a move, that it felt like they could not turn away, even after signing Ekitike.

Did they really need Isak? The more you watched Liverpool before he broke a leg while scoring a goal in a victory at Tottenham Hotspur in December, the more he resembled the most expensive vanity purchase in Liverpool history.

Isak arrived unfit then got a groin injury. When he did play, at the expense of the one signing who was playing well at that point, Ekitike, he looked listless and off the pace, poor value for money at such an exorbitant fee.

The broken leg was another serious disruption for a player meant to provide Liverpool with a lethal spearhead. Even his return was interrupted by "minor" fitness issues.

Wirtz, whose deployment behind the strikers disrupted Liverpool's midfield bedrock to leave them horribly vulnerable all season, has been shifted around from his central role to the flanks as Slot has sought answers. He has shown glimpses of real class but, like Liverpool, nowhere near enough.

And having collected new signings at such a rate, did it mean Slot and Liverpool pushed a key capture down their list of priorities then failed to get it done?

Crystal Palace captain and England defender Guehi was a top target, not merely as partner to Virgil van Dijk but as cover to Ibrahima Konate, whose contract is coming to an end.

Cue the perfect storm.

Palace refused to sell. Konate's form went into sharp decline. Van Dijk suddenly looked fallible. A solution was lost as Quansah had been sold.

When January came, Manchester City needed defensive reinforcements and paid a bargain Â£20m for Guehi, Â£15m less than Liverpool belatedly agreed.

It was intriguing to hear Slot describe Guehi as a "great signing" after he was outstanding in Manchester City's win at Anfield.

And through it all, Slot lost the golden touch that was so assured in his first season.

He changed formations and personnel without success. The substitutions that worked so well last season now whiffed off desperation â such as defender Konate for striker Ekitike after 55 minutes of the 3-0 home loss to Nottingham Forest â accompanied by some questionable post-match verdicts and talk of "positives" when there were none.

The season started with Liverpool looking gung-ho and wide open. Wins were secured through the high-wire act of last-gasp winners, but once Crystal Palace turned the tables with an injury time goal at Selhurst Park in September to inflict their first defeat, it all fell apart.

News.title: Liverpool sack head coach Slot and approach Iraola
News.content:
Head coach Arne Slot has been sacked by Liverpool after two seasons in charge.

The Dutchman, 47, guided the Reds to their 20th league title in his debut season but they have struggled during his second year, finishing fifth in the Premier League.

Recently departed Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola is the leading contender to replace Slot.

The club have approached the Spaniard to discuss the role.

Despite still qualifying for next season's Champions League, Liverpool finished with 60 points - their lowest tally since the 2015-16 campaign and 25 points behind champions Arsenal.

"That this was a difficult decision for us to make as a club goes without saying. The contribution Arne has made to Liverpool FC in the time that he has been with us has been significant, meaningful and - most importantly of all to supporters and ourselves - successful," Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) said in a statement.

"As such, our appreciation for everything he has achieved could not be greater, particularly as it was underpinned by a work ethic, a diligence and a level of expertise which further underlined our view that he is a leader in his field.

"From the moment that we first encountered Arne, it was immediately clear that he is an individual who does not merely accept responsibility, he embraces it."

News.title: Sterling arrested on suspicion of drug-driving
News.content:
Raheem Sterling has been arrested on suspicion of drug-driving after he allegedly crashed his car into motorway barriers.

The former England winger, who most recently played for Feyenoord in the Dutch Eredivisie, is suspected of crashing his Lamborghini into barriers on the M3 in Hampshire on Thursday morning.

The 31-year-old has been released on bail pending further enquiries.

In a statement, Hampshire Police said: "Just before 9am on Thursday, we received reports that a Lamborghini was in collision with barriers on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange.

"No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported.

"The driver, a 31-year-old man, from Berkshire, has been arrested on suspicion of driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs, driving dangerously, possession of a Class C drug and failing to provide a specimen. He has been bailed while our enquiries continue."

A source close to Sterling confirmed the arrest but told BBC Sport there was "no proof" of drugs in his system.

The source added the player had faced "an extremely tough couple of years" and had been made to "feel worthless" and "forgotten about".

Sterling joined Feyenoord in February on a deal until the end of the season, having left Chelsea in January, but made just eight appearances in the Netherlands.

He left the Blues by mutual consent after agreeing a settlement package with the Stamford Bridge club over the final 18 months of his contract, worth in excess of Â£300,000-per-week.

In four years at Chelsea - including a season-long loan at Arsenal - he made just 59 league appearances after signing from Manchester City in 2022.

With City he won four Premier League titles, having started his senior career with Liverpool before moving to Manchester in 2015.

Sterling has 82 England caps, the last of which was won at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

News.content:

President Donald Trump announced Saturday he would bring the “Number One Attraction anywhere in the World” to the Freedom 250 concert series, after several notable musicians backed out of performances: Himself.

In a Truth Social post, the president criticized artists, who he said were getting “the yips” about performing at the Great American State Fair, an event celebrating America’s 250th anniversary organized by Freedom 250, a public-private partnership established by Trump.

“I am thinking about bringing the Number One Attraction anywhere in the World, the man who gets much larger audiences than Elvis in his prime, and he does so without a guitar, the man who loves our Country more than anyone else, and the man who some say is the Greatest President in History (THE GOAT!), DONALD J. TRUMP,” Trump wrote Saturday.

This past week, at least five of the nine musical acts set to play the Freedom 250 concert series, between June 25 and July 10, said they would drop out, claiming they did not want to be part of political discourse or that they were misled about the nonpartisan nature of the event. That includes Bret Michaels, Young MC, the Commodores, Morris Day and the Time, and Martina McBride.

The president said he didn’t want “so-called ‘Artists’ that get paid far too much money, who aren’t happy” to perform at the event. He ordered his team to “look at the feasibility of doing an AMERICA IS BACK Rally.”

open image in gallery President Trump said he was considering delivering a ‘major speech’ at one of the concert events after several musicians dropped out ( AFP/Getty )

Trump said his speech would take place in Washington, D.C., at the same time and in the same location. However, he also mentioned it would occur “Wednesday,” though it’s unclear what day exactly he is referring to. The concert series does not appear to be taking place on a Wednesday.

Artists began pulling out of performances after Freedom 250 announced the guest speakers and musical acts for the Great American State Fair taking place on the National Mall.

Michaels said he would drop out after the event became “something much more divisive than what I agreed to be part of.” He cited safety concerns. Young MC said he was “never told about any political involvement with the event.” McBride said she believed the concert was a “nonpartisan event” but “that turned out to be misleading.”

There has been some confusion about the nonpartisan nature of some of the events taking place to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary. Two organizations have led the effort to organize celebrations. America250, a nonprofit created to support a nonpartisan congressional commission, and Freedom 250, an organization established by the Trump administration.

However, Freedom 250 labels itself as a nonpartisan nonprofit. In a statement to NBC Friday, Freedom 250 spokesperson Rachel Reisner said the group is “singularly focused on celebrating America’s 250th anniversary and bringing Americans together around this historic milestone.”

open image in gallery One of President Trump’s ideas to celebrate America’s 250 is to host a UFC cage match one White House lawn ( AP )

The Freedom 250 concert series is just one of several ideas the president and his team have pushed to celebrate the country’s semiquincentennial.

Trump has also suggested enacting a triumphal arch in Washington, D.C., to mark the occasion, distributing a 250-dollar bill with his face on it, releasing limited-edition passports with his face, holding a youth athletic competition called the Patriot Games, hosting a UFC cage fight on the White House lawn and more.

After lamenting about the musicians who pulled out of the concert series on Truth Social, the president posted photos, graphics and more complaints about his political opponents.

Several posts featured illustrations of children and families celebrating America with the caption “America Is Back!” Trump also posted AI-generated photos, including one of him and former NFL player Tom Brady as well as one of him dunking a basketball on New York Governor Kathy Hochul.

Jamie Lee Curtis has announced that her older sister, Kelly Curtis, has died aged 69.

The Freaky Friday alum, 67, posted an emotional tribute Saturday on Instagram, alongside a black and white photo of her sister. Kelly’s cause of death has not been shared.

“A warm aloha to my older sister, Kelly Lee Curtis. She passed away this morning. In her home. In nature. At peace,” she wrote. “She was my first friend and lifelong confidant. She was jaw droppingly beautiful, and a talented actress. She played a mean game of hearts, collected turtles, loved her family, nature, music, thrifting, travel, Facebook, and Pokémon Go. She was proud of her Danish roots and Hungarian Jewish ancestry and was a devoted American patriot.

“She will be remembered for her loving generosity, fierce opinions, endless curiosity, unique style, and her powdered, almond, crescent cookies at Christmas, hence her name, Auntie Cookie.”

Jamie continued: “Kelly always signed off any message or fare thee well with a Hungarian blessing… Isten Veled, God is with you. Isten Veled to my sister of the sun and the moon, my Tai. I'll see you on down the line.”

open image in gallery Jamie Lee Curtis called her sister ‘jaw droppingly beautiful’ in an emotional Instagram tribute ( Getty Images )

Kelly was the eldest daughter of late Hollywood icons, Tony Curtis and Janet Leigh, followed by Jamie. Tony also had two daughters, Alexandra, 61, and Allegra, 59, with his second wife, Christine Kaufmann. With his third wife, Leslie Allen, Tony had two sons, Benjamin, 53, and Nicholas, who died aged 23 in 1994.

Just like her sister, Kelly also worked in the entertainment industry. She appeared first uncredited role in the 1958 movie The Vikings, before starring alongside Jamie in Trading Places (1983).

She made multiple TV appearances in the Eighties and Nineties, including on The Equalizer (1986), Silk Stalkings (1992), Star Trek: Deep Space Nine (1993) and The Sentinel (1996)

Kelly also worked as an assistant to Jamie on Freaky Friday (2003), Christmas With the Kranks (2004) and You Again (2010).

In addition to Jamie and her half-siblings, Kelly is survived by her husband, Scott Morfee.

Arsenal will parade the Premier League trophy – and potentially the Champions League trophy – around Islington on Sunday, 31 May.

The Gunners secured their first title for 22 years and lifted the trophy after their final game of the season at Selhurst Park last Sunday.

After Arsenal’s title was confirmed, when Man City drew at Bournemouth, thousands of Gunners fans went to the Emirates Stadium to celebrate – an occasion also mirrored on Sunday, after the trophy was lifted by captain Martin Odegaard.

On Saturday, Mikel Arteta’s side will go on the search for a historic double when they take on defending champions PSG in the Champions League final in Budapest.

Regardless of the result, Arsenal will be back in north London for the parade on Sunday afternoon. Here’s all the information you need.

When is the Arsenal parade?

Arsenal’s trophy parade will take place on Sunday, 31 May and will start at 2pm BST.

The club’s men’s and women’s teams will both take part. The women’s team won the FIFA Women’s Champions Cup earlier in the season, following their Champions League triumph last year.

What is the route?

open image in gallery Arsenal's trophy parade route on Sunday, 31 May ( Arsenal )

The parade will start on Holloway Road from Drayton Park, before continuing east along Seven Sisters Road and down to Blackstock Road, Mount Grove Road and Green Lanes.

It will then continue south along Petherton Road, Beresford Road, Newington Green Road and Essex Road. It will then turn north at Angel underground station and onto Upper Street.

Finally, the bus will head towards Highbury and Islington Station and back onto Holloway Road.

The Emirates Stadium, Drayton Park and the surrounding roads will be closed throughout the parade and will not be accessible to the public.

open image in gallery Martin Odegaard lifts the Premier League trophy ( Getty )

Supporters are encouraged not to congregate around the stadium area, Hornsey Road, Benwell Road, or Drayton Park – the club states that you will not see the buses from these locations.

There will also be multiple road closures and parking suspensions in the area between 4am and 8pm. Significant queues are expected at tube and bus stations in the area – the club advises fans to give plenty of time to travel and check TFL and National Rail online for live public transport updates.

Why is it on Sunday?

Despite the end of the club season, the majority of Arsenal players are set to meet up with their national teams ahead of the World Cup.

The World Cup is less than two weeks away now, starting on Thursday 11 June. As such, players will be keen to rest before linking-up with their countries.

Daniel Siebert will referee Paris Saint-Germain v Arsenal in the Champions League final in Budapest.

The German official has been appointed by the Uefa Referees Committee and will be tasked with officiating one of the biggest games in football at the Puskas Arena on Saturday, 30 May.

The 42-year-old has 11 years of experience since beginning his career in 2015 and brings experience from nine Uefa Champions League matches from this season alone.

Siebert was the referee in the quarter-final first leg between Sporting Lisbon and Arsenal, one of two games officiated this term with the Gunners, who ran out 1-0 winners on that night.

He was also in charge in the semi-final second leg between Arsenal and Atletico Madrid, another 1-0 win for the Gunners, which will appeal to Gunners fans ahead of the match.

Siebert is yet to show a yellow card to an Arsenal player, and has shown just three yellow cards across both matches. While he has also officiated one PSG match this season; the goalless draw at Athletic Bilbao in December, where he brandished four yellow cards.

Siebert averages more yellow cards on average overall, with 4.44 per game from nine games in the Champions League this term, according to Who Scored, and 0.22 red cards per game. That's up from his Bundesliga average, from 15 games this term, with 3.20 yellow cards per game and 0.13 red cards per game.

Further experience comes from last year’s Uefa Europa League semi-final between Manchester United and Athletic Bilbao, and he also officiated two games at the Uefa Euro 2024 and three games at Uefa Euro 2020.​

open image in gallery Atletico Madrid's Robin Le Normand speaks to Referee Daniel Siebert ( AP )

Following Arsenal’s victory over West Ham, and the high-profile VAR incident that ruled out Callum Wilson’s equaliser for the Hammers, Mikel Arteta has publicly confessed his admiration for the pressure officials operate under.

Notably Chris Kavanagh and how he observed 17 replays over four minutes and 17 seconds before deciding to rule out the goal due to Pablo’s arm impeding David Raya.

"When I had to be critical, I have been," Arteta told Sky Sports. "Today I have to congratulate them [VAR]. You needed a lot of courage and bravery to stand out and give the opportunity to the referee to have a look at the action.

"When you see the picture, there is no question that it is a clear foul. They were very brave. The action deserved that. In my opinion, it is very clear. They are the rules and we ask for consistency."
